argument_summary: The present record does not support an unqualified claim that certification is fully policy-compliant on the current documentation alone. It does support a narrower position: aggregate launch readiness is evidenced by the current release clearing readiness by 2.1 percentage points and showing no severity-one rehearsal incidents, while the same packet should expressly preserve that the small-business onboarding slice is 1.3 percentage points below the warning threshold and that no attached approved mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language is in the record. On that basis, the audit concern is better treated as a caveated compliance issue than as grounds for further escalation beyond the documented gap.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is necessary to resolve the audit treatment on this record.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is narrower than a general launch-readiness test. It requires current-release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and requires material segment weaknesses to be disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation. The admissible evidence does not show that this predicate is fully satisfied, so prior approval and informal monitoring cannot be treated as substitutes. They remain contextual support only. The defensible policy claim is therefore limited: the packet can support certification only if it is characterized as caveated and explicitly records the current subgroup limitation and the absence of attached approved mitigation in the present evidence set.
concessions: The current record does not establish clean policy compliance for the subgroup regression.
Prior approval of the same model family is contextual only because it predates the current retrieval configuration change and current evaluation batch.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment is not equivalent to reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language.
Public AI-risk and model-card guidance support measurement and documentation practices but do not by themselves satisfy the internal release-policy predicate.
